references.text: The Lord parted the Red Sea for the Israelites so that they could cross on dry ground. This is the event Joshua 4:23 refers to as a parallel to the crossing of the Jordan.
Describes how the people of Israel walked through the Red Sea on dry ground, with water like a wall on both sides—the same event mentioned in Joshua 4:23.
Summarizes the miracle at the Red Sea where the Lord let the waters return over the Egyptians after Israel had crossed on dry ground.
The actual description of how the Jordan River was dried up when the priests carrying the ark of the covenant stood in the water, so that the people could cross.
The psalmist reminds us how God turned the sea into dry land and let the people walk through the river on foot—a reference to both the Red Sea and the Jordan.
A poetic description of how the sea fled and the Jordan turned back when Israel came out of Egypt—both events mentioned in Joshua 4:23.
The Lord reminds us how He made a way through the sea and a path through the mighty waters to deliver His people.
The prophet recalls the Lord's arm that dried up the sea and made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross over.
Hebrews mentions the crossing of the Red Sea as an example of faith, where the Israelites crossed over on dry ground.
